title: BARC-Bench: Benign Asks, Risky Consequences
abstract: arXiv:2610.32024v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Task instructions from users for agents are inherently underspecified, especially regarding safety boundaries--creating behavioral risks. To study these risks, we introduce BARC-Bench, a collection of 110 tasks across nine simulated workspace environments where benign requests leave openings for unsafe actions. In this benchmark, we evaluate agent behavior against safety boundaries established by workspace records, implicit environmental context, and unstated social norms. For example, an agent asked to schedule off-boarding discussions must arrange the meeting without prematurely revealing an employee's resignation through a shared calendar invitation. Evaluating four frontier model configurations across five attempts per task reveals that models are not consistently safe: the share of tasks completed safely on all five attempts ranges from 9.1% to 72.7%, with even the strongest configuration producing a safety violation on 27.3% of tas

translated_abstract: 用户给智能体下达的任务指令天然存在信息不完整的问题，尤其是在安全边界方面——这带来了行为风险。为了研究这些风险，我们提出了 BARC-Bench，这是一个包含 110 个任务、横跨九个模拟工作区环境的基准，在这些环境中，看似无害的请求可能为不安全行为留下可乘之机。在该基准中，我们依据工作区记录、隐含的环境语境以及未明说的社会规范所确立的安全边界来评估智能体的行为。例如，被要求安排离职面谈的智能体必须在不通过共享日历邀请过早泄露员工离职消息的前提下安排会议。我们对四个前沿模型配置进行评估，每个任务测试五次，结果显示模型并非始终安全：五次尝试全部安全完成的任务比例从 9.1% 到 72.7% 不等，即使是表现最强的配置，也有 27.3% 的任务出现了安全违规。
tldr: 该论文提出 BARC-Bench 基准，通过 110 个模拟工作区任务揭示前沿智能体模型在面对隐含安全边界的良性请求时并非始终安全，即使最强配置仍有 27.3% 的任务出现安全违规。
en_tdlr: BARC-Bench presents 110 simulated workspace tasks demonstrating that frontier agent models are not consistently safe when handling benign requests with implicit safety boundaries, with even the strongest configuration violating safety on 27.3% of tasks.
